incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: unusual auth traffic pattern detected. auth-proxy edges reporting mirrored requests (identical payloads) across 5 regions from 3.94.12.0/22 and 18.211.4.0/24. Multiple service tokens used. Possible log-forwarding or exfil. Automatic rate limit engaged.
ben_sre: Oncall here, digging in. Which service tokens are implicated?
alice.ops: Saw entries for svc-edge-forwarder and svc-logs-ingest. Correlating with Kinesis forwarder failures.
irina_security: Copy. Can we confirm if any S3 put events correlate? If keys leaked we need rotation ASAP.
ben_sre: Querying logs... `jq '.token_id' /tmp/auth-sample.log | sort | uniq -c` shows repeated token ids: `sf-87d` and `lf-21a` used ~16k times last hour.
ben_sre: I'm going to add a temporary ACL on the edge layer for those prefixes and disable the forwarder role. Will post commands.
alice.ops: Command to block prefix (edge fw):
```
# block CIDR at edge ingress
rtrctl deny add prefix 3.94.12.0/22 reason "suspected-exfil"
rtrctl deny add prefix 18.211.4.0/24 reason "suspected-exfil"
```
alice.ops: Done — propagated to 5 regions. :white_check_mark:
irina_security: Good. Next: rotate svc-edge-forwarder keys. Who owns the service account creds?
ben_sre: Owner shows `svc-edge-forwarder` (team: infra-logging). I'm triggering rotation via deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: rotation triggered for svc-edge-forwarder -> job 8721. Key versions queued: v7 -> v8. Old keys will be revoked in 5 minutes.
tess_support: Heads up: We're preparing customer comms for any app-facing errors. Any SLO impact expected?
leo_prod: Early indicators: some clients showing 502s where requests hit blocked prefixes; customers with strict IP allowlists may see transient failures. No data exfil confirmed yet.
irina_security: Action checklist:
- Contain: blocked CIDRs (done)
- Rotate: svc-edge-forwarder keys (in progress)
- Audit: identify any S3 puts by those tokens -> run `aws s3api list-objects --query ...`
- Notify legal if PII suspected
ben_sre: Audit snippet: found 23 s3 PUTs to `redwood-logs-temp` from ip 3.94.12.23 between 02:14-02:18 UTC. Investigating contents.
alice.ops: I spun up a forensic bucket copy and disabled public access. `aws s3api get-object --bucket redwood-logs-temp --key suspect/2026-03-17.tar.gz /tmp/suspect.tar.gz` (downloading for triage)
irina_security: If those objects contain customer logs, escalate legal and privacy. For now limit access to sec+legal.
tess_support: I'll draft a short customer status note: "We detected anomalous activity affecting auth proxies. We have blocked suspicious IPs and rotated impacted credentials. We're investigating potential log forwarding; no confirmed customer data exposure at this time." Will share draft in #customer-communications.
ben_sre: Rotation complete, old keys revoked. `deploy-bot` reports success and no rollout failures. :lock:
deploy-bot: rotation job 8721 completed: 0 failed, new key v8 active.
irina_security: Good. Preserve evidence: snapshot `/var/log/auth-proxy/2026-03-17-02*.log` saved to secure forensics host. Hashes computed.
alice.ops: Forensics uploaded. `sha256`: 9f3b...edc2
leo_prod: I've flagged top-10 potentially impacted customers to CS. No customer facing outage declared yet.
irina_security: Next steps: full S3 object inspection and token lineage. If we confirm PII, notify customers per policy. Otherwise we close as contained and rotate.
ben_sre: Handoff: I'm going offline in 40m. Tess, please take ownership for monitoring and followup. I'll leave runbook notes.
tess_support: Taking over. Monitoring dashboards pinned. Will update every 30m or on material findings. :handshake:
irina_security: Thanks team. Marking incident state: CONTAINED -> keys rotated, CIDRs blocked, forensic capture complete. Investigations ongoing. Will open a postmortem ticket.
ben_sre: filing incident ticket 2026-INC-3024 with timeline and artifacts.
